doc.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Big band work and Earl Hines
summary: He did little big band work but played with Earl Hines in a quartet and a Riverboat big band, filling in for Oliver Jackson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: When you, you kind of caught the tail end of the heyday of the big bands I guess, after they kind of had a tough time after World War II. Did you get to do much big band playing because of that?

I didn’t do too much big band, very little big band myself, except like I said if I played some local dances. But I did have a chance to play with one big band that I enjoyed. They assembled a big band for Earl Fatha Hines, and we played at the Riverboat. And I did a week of that with him and then I went on to do something else. But that was wonderful. Well I had been out with Earl for a while. We had dome some quartet things. Oliver Jackson, my wonderful friend Oliver who is gone now — I sure miss him also, he was a great drummer. Oliver was with Earl at the time, and he was going to go with Kenny Burrell for a while. And so he asked me would I, and I say sure. He said, “Earl would like you to come and play.” So I went with Earl for a while. We move around like that. That’s the beautiful part about music, you know. You get different experiences working with different people. So I worked with Earl, Budd Johnson, Bill Pendleton and myself and we had a wonderful time with the quartet. We went everywhere. So after we did a tour of the states, most of the states, Earl was getting ready to go to Russia so he asked me if I would like to go. I said, “Well now, Earl, Oliver should be coming back to make that tour.” He said, “Well if he doesn’t, you know if he’s tied up, you know you’re welcome, you can do it if you want to.” I said I was very appreciative of that. I said that’s great, thanks. I said well Oliver’s going to come back and he’s going to go to Russia and do that tour. And I went and did some other things and but we did, before I left we did have a chance to do a big band thing down at the Riverboat Room in New York. And that was nice. The good thing about that, Ella Fitzgerald was also on the bill with her group, Ed Thigpen was the drummer with her, and it was great, and so it was the two groups. And after that I did occasional big band things with maybe if Buck had a dance or something like that, or somebody you know, a commercial, some leader would call me for a date, a club date type thing with a big band.
